newsitem.title: UK: Oct Brent loadings up at 44 cargoes plus top-ups.
newsitem.headline: Oct Brent loadings up at 44 cargoes plus top-ups.

text.p: October's U.K. North Sea Brent Blend crude loading programme will consist of 44 full 500,000-barrel cargoes and an additional 1.43 million barrels in top-up cargoes, traders said.
The Brent volumes scheduled to load in October were 1.03 million barrels more than the original September programme of 41 full cargoes and an additional 1.9 million barrels in top-ups.
September saw maintenance work at the Hudson platform, operated by Amerada Hess, and at Shell Expro's Cormorant Alpha and Tern and at Chevron's South Ninian platform.

Apart from a long-term redevelopment project at Shell's Brent Charlie, which continues until the end of the year, October maintenance will be limited to a seven-day shutdown of Shell's 36,000 barrels per day (bpd) North Cormorant platform.
Brent Blend, created by blending crude produced from the Brent and Ninian systems, is loaded from the northern Scottish terminal of Sullom Voe in the Shetland Islands.
Brent is one of the world's most widely traded spot market crudes and therefore is used as a benchmark to price many other internationally traded grades.
